newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian rebels blast pipeline, pollute river.
newsitem.headline: Colombian rebels blast pipeline, pollute river.

text.p: Leftist rebels have dynamited Colombia's second largest pipeline, spilling crude oil into a nearby river and halting pumping operations, the state oil company Ecopetrol said on Thursday.

Company officials said National Liberation Army (ELN) rebels carried out the attack on Wednesday night on a section of the Colombia Pipeline close to the town of Remedios in the northwestern province of Antioquia.
It was the 10th time this year that guerrillas have blasted the pipeline, which runs through the centre of the country and transports 150,000 barrels a day.
No estimate was available for the latest spillage but in the previous nine attacks more than 19,200 barrels of crude were lost, Ecopetrol officials said.
An Ecopetrol spokeswoman said oil spilled into the San Pedro river after the blast and caused localised pollution.

The attack followed the arrest of 14 men in the past week on charges of blowing up oil pipelines and of links to the ELN. Eleven of them are members of Colombia's main oil union, the USO, including its national treasurer Cesar Carrillo.
The arrests sparked a strike call by the USO but the union took no further action pending talks with the government.
